Sara — thanks, sending the technical summary below and the attachments as discussed. Short version up front: Redwood offers a contractual and technical "no-train" guarantee for customers who elect exclusion; we enforce it through tenant-level flags, separate telemetry routing, and immutable audit logs. Details follow.

1) No-train attestation (summary):
- Contract: DPA addendum + "no-train" rider. When a customer signs the rider, the customer's tenant is marked with an internal "no_train=true" flag and that status is propagated to the inference routing layer.
- Technical enforcement: requests from no-train tenants are routed to inference endpoints with training-disabled mode; we disable all model updates, do not feed prompts or outputs into offline training stores, and set ephemeral cache TTLs for tenant data.
- Auditability: every change to a tenant's no_train flag produces an append-only audit event (timestamp, actor, request id) stored in an immutable audit ledger and mirrored to customer-specific export buckets for at-rest export.

2) Tenant export sample (attachment: redacted_tenant_export_sample.csv):
- Format: CSV with columns [timestamp, tenant_id, event_type, request_id, no_train_flag, route, storage_ttl_seconds].
- Example row (redacted):
  2027-05-08T22:14:10Z, tenant-REDACTED, auth.request, req-REDACTED, true, inference-llm-01, 172800
- We will provide a sanitized sample scoped to the last 30 days showing both the flag set and the audit events.

3) Dataflow diagram (attachment: llm_dataflow_diagram.pdf):
- Includes: ingress (API / SDK), real-time routing, ephemeral KV cache (48h default for non-persistent prompts), inference runtime, logging subsystem, metrics telemetry, backups, and subprocessors (object storage, logging platform, analytics).
- Note: ephemeral KV cache is memory-first, encrypted in-transit; we persist only minimal metadata for observability (non-PII) by default. Full prompt/response storage is only enabled when the customer opts into "persistence" or for Dedicated deployments where they manage storage.

4) SCC mapping (attachment: scc_mapping.xlsx) + EU data transfers: 
- We have signed SCCs with our cloud provider and include a mapping sheet that ties inference flows to SCC clauses. For EU-resident customers, routing policy can keep data in EU regions; if cross-border replication is required, we list subprocessors and legal basis.

5) SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ references:
- SOC 2 report (link): https://redwood.example.com/soc2/report/latest (we provide to customers under NDA).
- SIG/CAIQ: the attached workbook includes our SIG short-form responses and a CAIQ matrix excerpt that calls out controls for model training and data segregation.

6) Evidence generation & timeline:
- Export & paperwork: we will deliver the redacted tenant export + attachments by Wed EOD (2027-05-12).
- Sample export will be redacted to remove any clinical PHI; if ClearPort requires raw export under an executed DPA, we will follow the DPA export process.

Attachments included: [redacted_tenant_export_sample.csv], [llm_dataflow_diagram.pdf], [scc_mapping.xlsx], [dpo_affidavit.docx] (DPO-level attestation).

If you want a short technical call to walk the privacy team through the diagram and export format, propose times and we'll set it up.

Thanks,
